# [mods] Rear drum-to-disc brake swap

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Source an 88-95 Pathfinder rear axle assembly and swap it onto Xterra front or rear axle shafts. [t1134]

Swap rear drum brakes to disc by removing the ABS ring and installing new axle studs. [t1134]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Source a rear axle assembly from an 88-95 Pathfinder with coil springs and H233 axles.
2. Remove the entire backing plate, caliper, rotor, and brake line assembly by cutting the hard lines and parking brake cables.
3. Transfer the disc brake backing plates to Xterra front or rear axle shafts using a special removal tool (Nissan J-45073) if not buying pre-assembled units.
4. [Partial] Press out the original 31-spline Pathfinder axle shafts from their backing plates, noting that this requires significant force and new bearings for the Xterra.
5. Remove the bearing cups from the transferred backing plates by driving out short mounting studs or using a shop press on about half of them.
6. Clean and paint the backing plates to remove rusted dust shields before installing the new hardware.
7. [Partial] Drill 13/64 holes in the driver's side plate and tap with a 6mm x 1.0 thread to accept Xterra-specific parking brake cables.
8. Install new bearings, seals, lock washers, and ABS tone rings onto the axle shafts before mounting them back into the truck.

_Procedure reported by [t1134]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Build the Xterra axle shafts on a work bench before tearing into the truck to avoid rebuilding the drum parking brake. [t1134]
- Save the retaining washer and nut from disassembly for reassembly; discard only the lock washer. [t1134]
- Use a stack of washers when pulling in shouldered studs to ensure full thread engagement. [t1134]
- Cut shoe nails on old drum shoes if keeping them, allowing them to collapse off the axle during removal. [t1134]

## Common mistakes

- Forgetting that two backing plate studs may be too short for a deep parking brake housing. [t1134]
